"Root, or administrator, is the highest level of authority on a system: it can stop any process and change anything. Precisely because of that, good practice is to hand it out as rarely as possible and for as short a time as possible. \"Root admin\" is shorthand for the access level, not a job title."
"Three attack lanes feeding the core server"
"Applies to every {0} in every match from now on, on top of CORE FIRMWARE. Early levels are cheap; each one costs more than the last, and the top levels cost millions."
"Linked, but Google could not be reached. Nothing is lost — the save on this device is the one being played, and the next sync catches the account up."
"Hostile code disguised as something you asked for. Slow to move but heavily wrapped — armour blunts every individual hit, so fast weak shots waste themselves on it."
"Pick a difficulty to see its worldwide board."
"Everything owned, revives included, comes back from Google Play with RESTORE on any device. It is never part of the cloud save, so no save file can grant or take away a purchase."
"Code that abuses a specific flaw in a system. Exploits move fast and hit hard; detection range matters more than raw damage when these are inbound."

"Deals no damage of its own. Buffs every agent in range by +30% damage and +20% fire rate, so its value is entirely in where you put it."

"Network architects design how a network is divided up. Segmentation means a compromise in one area cannot simply walk into the next, which limits the damage of any single failure. It is design work done before an incident, not a tool used during one."
"Saving the soundtrack needs Android 10 or newer."
"A grid whose cells warm and cool with the traffic."
"ANALYST does 80% extra to elites. Armour-ignoring agents help."
"Counts as encrypted: most agents land reduced damage."
"Spend it on permanent CORE FIRMWARE damage."
"Place two TARPITs so their auras cover the ground your FIREWALLs are shooting at. Slowing is what makes the damage land."
"A coarse grid whose cells warm and cool with the traffic."
"This erases your saved run, every unlocked agent, all statistics and your settings.\n\nThis cannot be undone."
"Bosses move slowly but hit CORE-SERVER for {0} integrity. They pay out the most crypto in the game, and they get tougher every cycle."

"A cyber operations specialist runs defence as a live operation: watching for interference, keeping the team's tools working while someone is actively trying to switch them off, and going straight at the source of it."
"Its contents are scrambled, so most defences cannot read what they are shooting at and only land partial damage. A CRYPTOGRAPHER agent cuts straight through the cipher."
"BOSS {0} OF {1} · TAP A BOSS TO SWITCH"
"CRT phosphor green, scanlines and a refresh sweep."
"Focus fire. ANALYST and ROOT ADMIN carry boss waves."
"Reliable mid-range damage at a low price, and the only agent immune to a boss JAM. Short reach, so it has to stand close to the lane — which is exactly why that immunity matters."
"ONE AD AFTER A LOST RUN · REVIVE OPT-IN"
"Armoured and patient. Heavy single hits beat it; rapid fire wastes itself."
"Sparse columns of falling characters behind the field."

"An Intrusion Prevention System sits in the traffic path and is permitted to act on what it detects, dropping or resetting a connection rather than only alerting. The trade-off is real: an IPS that misjudges legitimate traffic blocks it."
"A firewall checks traffic against a list of rules and drops anything that does not match. It is the oldest and still the most important perimeter defence there is."
"Slow diagonal data currents crossing the field."

"This game was developed with assistance from artificial intelligence tools, used as educational and development aids while learning programming and software development.

AI tools assisted with areas such as code development, troubleshooting, documentation and learning. Final design decisions, gameplay direction, testing and publication decisions remain the responsibility of the developer.

This game is not generated, sponsored, endorsed, owned or published by any artificial intelligence company."
"Gets back up once, at 40% health. Killing it is not the same as finishing it."
"Unlock this agent by reaching wave {0} on {1}."
"Anything kills these. Do not over-build for them."
"Overwhelming single-target damage that ignores all armour. The most expensive agent in the game and unlocked very late. Exposes the targeting selector."
"Cheap and nearly harmless. Everything inside its radius crawls."

"The countdown keeps running while this is open."
"This build shows advertisements supplied by Google AdMob. Watching an ad to continue a run is always optional and is never required to play."

"A tarpit accepts a hostile connection and then answers as slowly as it is allowed to, holding the attacker open on a socket that is going nowhere. It is a delaying tactic, not a blocking one: the value is the time it costs the other side."
"Every hit speeds it up, however small; it slows when left alone. Few big hits beat many small ones."
"ZERO-DAY HUNTER and ROOT ADMIN ignore armour entirely."
"GRADIENT speeds up with every hit, however small, and slows when left alone. Few big hits beat many small ones."
"Also start boss waves automatically. Off: boss waves wait for you"
"Your waves, agents, € and firmware are saved to your Google account. Sign into it on another device and they are there. It syncs when you leave the game and when a run ends."
"Halve the frame rate and drop decorative effects"
"A zero-day is a vulnerability the defender has had zero days to fix, because nobody knew it existed. There is no signature to match against, which is what makes them so dangerous."
"Google Play answered. Purchases and restores work normally."
"Banked at every tenth wave. The deeper a run goes, the more it pays — the award grows with the square of the milestone, so one deep run beats five shallow ones."
"Tap two highlighted deployment nodes beside a route. Two is not a suggestion: one agent cannot cover a lane on its own."
"Stored locally on this device · nothing is uploaded"
"Pinch with two fingers to zoom in on the board — nodes are easier to tap up close. While zoomed, drag with one finger to move around. Pinch all the way out to see the whole board again."
"BOTMASTER drops BOTs behind itself every few seconds. Kill it fast, and keep something for the swarm."
"No gambling, loot boxes or randomised paid rewards"

"Armour blunts small hits: bring ANALYST or ROOT ADMIN, not IPS."
"LOCKED · Complete level 5 (clear wave 100 on DDoS) to unlock the music player and the track list."

"A firewall checks traffic against a set of rules and drops anything the rules do not allow. It is usually the first control placed between an untrusted network and something worth protecting, and it is judged on the rules it is given rather than on cleverness."
"Heavy single-target damage, identical on every shot rather than a gamble, and it ignores armour. Expensive and slow; one of these does not hold a lane on its own."
"It also raises the ◇ crypto every run pays out, +{0}% per level up to double. It does not affect enemy health or wave composition."
"Cyberattacks are inbound on CORE-SERVER. Deploy Cyber Agents beside the routes to stop them before they land."
"Linked. Sign into the same Google account on another phone or tablet and your progress is there."
"KERNEL PANIC jams every agent within reach for 3 seconds when it dies. FIREWALL stands in it."
"Thousands of machines send traffic at one target at once. No single request is an attack; the flood is. The goal is not to break in, it is to make the service unusable."
"Keep it under fire: it only repairs after a moment unhit, so cover the gaps between kill zones."
"Google Play Games could not be reached. Your runs are recorded on this device and your best is posted next time a run ends while you are online."
"The collection run. No tricks, no jamming — twenty per cent more of it than anything else on the board."

"The rack your core is built into. Seen on the battlefield."
"A bloated model: a little more health, a little slower."

"Fictional licence, clearly flagged: this agent simply ignores the ENCRYPTED trait instead of being slowed by it, and deals triple damage to anything carrying it. Real cryptography does not work this way and nothing here breaks any real cipher."
"Wave {0} and everything deployed will be lost."
"Select an agent, then tap a highlighted deployment node."
"Compromised computers quietly taking orders from a central controller. Their owners usually have no idea. Botnets are what make large DDoS attacks possible."
"An attack against a flaw nobody has patched yet — the defender has had zero days to prepare. Rare, tough, and worth real crypto to shut down."
"Permanent upgrades · every match from now on"

"Breaks into three smaller worms when killed, and each of those breaks once more. Splash is your friend."

"Data sent across a network is chopped into packets: small chunks with a destination address and a payload. A packet is not an attack — almost all of them are ordinary traffic. What you shoot here are packets carrying a specific attack, which is why each one is named for the attack rather than for the packet."
"3 revives per run and no revive ads ever, plus €5,000."
"No real cryptocurrency, blockchain, wallet, mining or NFTs"
"Asking Google Play what this account owns. This usually takes a moment."
"When it dies, every agent near it is jammed for 3 seconds. Kill it far from your board, or with the next wave far off."
"Spread your agents out so one jam cannot silence the line."
"ANONYMOUS HACK — {0} BOTS INCOMING AT DOUBLE SPEED"
"Nothing else is sent anywhere. The game is playable with no network at all."

"Slow, heavy hits. +80% damage to elites and bosses."
"Ignores encryption entirely and deals triple damage to it."

"A \"blue team\" defends a system and responds to incidents — the counterpart to a red team. \"Blue hat\" is used in more than one way in the industry and is not a standardised term, so only the blue team meaning is described here."
"Splitting a network so a breach in one area cannot reach the rest. It is why one compromised laptop should not mean a compromised company."
"Battery saver only changes what is drawn. Wave difficulty, damage and timing are completely unaffected."
"Purchases, restores and what leaves this device"

"IPS does 35% extra to swarms. Position it where lanes converge."
"Deletes your saved run, unlocked agents, statistics and settings. This cannot be undone."
"Casts decoy copies of itself that soak up fire. ANALYST and ROOT ADMIN see through them."
"Fires as fast as anything in the roster and always shoots a boss first. Double damage to [GG] GOOD GAME. Four maximum."

"A senior security engineer with a bachelor's degree in cyber security, who stops attacks by building the software that defends against them: hardened services, patches and filters that are in place before the attack arrives rather than after it."

"Builds a wall across the nearest route within its range. Threats stop at the wall and have to break it down before they can pass; bosses break it fastest. When it falls, ACE rebuilds it after a few seconds, stronger with every level. Its own shots deal {0}× damage to every boss of the first five levels. No more than three may be deployed."
"Every few seconds, locks one agent's upgrades for 8 seconds. Upgrade before it arrives."
"This is the attack wave you are facing. It climbs for as long as you hold the server — every fifth wave brings a boss."

"Two different things get called \"quantum\" in security and they are worth keeping apart. Quantum key distribution uses physics to detect eavesdropping on a link, and is deployed only in rare, specialised settings. Post-quantum cryptography is ordinary software maths designed to resist future quantum computers, and is the one actually being rolled out."

"A blind injection gets no error messages back, so the attacker infers the answer one true-or-false question at a time. It is slower and far more patient than a normal injection, and it arrives hardened against the obvious defences."
"First tap shows the agent's range on that spot; tap it again to deploy"
"One route slashes corner to corner across the board five times."
"Buffs every agent in range: +30% damage, +20% fire rate."

"The most common attack on the internet, and the baseline threat here. An attacker types database commands into a field that expected a name or a password; if the application passes that straight through, the database obeys."
"Hides for 2 seconds of every 6: nothing can target it. Splash and chains still reach it."
"OTHER: small units and elites only, never bosses"

"Very long detection range; +45% damage to fast attacks."

"A single compromised machine taking orders from someone else. One bot is harmless. A botnet of thousands is not — which is why these always arrive in groups."

"Every agent inside its range, itself included, is immune to jamming from any boss. Fast, heavy shots, with {0}× damage to WHITE EYE and BLACK EYE. TARPIT's range. No more than two may be deployed."

"Real traffic follows a route through switches and routers to reach its destination. The two serpentine routes here are that path, doubling back so you can see every hop at once."

"CORE-SERVER is what you are defending, and its INTEGRITY readout in the top strip is the only life you have. Every hostile packet that reaches the rack takes a bite out of it. At 0 the server is breached and the run ends — so nothing gets through is the whole job."
"ROOTKIT hides for 2 seconds of every 6 and nothing can target it. Splash and chains still reach it."

"Applications ask databases questions in SQL. If user input is pasted straight into that question, an attacker can write their own ending to it — dumping a user table, bypassing a login, or deleting the lot. The fix is old and well known (parameterised queries), which is what makes it so frustrating that it is still the attack you will meet most often."

"An Intrusion Detection System watches network or host activity for patterns that look like an attack and raises an alert. It reports; it does not block. Someone, or something else, still has to act on what it finds."
"ON THE FIELD · TAP A BOSS TO SEE IT"
"Lean on non-FIREWALL agents for this wave."
"Begin the next wave automatically after a short pause"

"Cryptography protects data in transit and at rest, so that intercepting it is not the same as reading it. Attackers use it too — a lot of hostile traffic is encrypted — which is why defenders inspect at endpoints they control rather than trying to break the encryption itself."
"A circuit lattice that breathes with the wave."
"Purchases are tied to your Google account, not to this device. Reinstalling or changing phone does not lose them."

"A \"red team\" attacks a system with permission, to find what an attacker would find first. \"Red hat\" is informal slang rather than a job title or a certification, and its meaning varies between people who use it; the red team half is the part that is standard."
"Each player's best wave, worldwide, listed by callsign. Register one on the right, or Google shows your Play Games name instead."
"Heavy single-target damage, identical every shot. Ignores all armour."

"This build has no advertising to configure."

"Fires as fast as the hats and hits harder, with {0}× damage to the DUCK-USB bosses SYN-STORM and GRADIENT. Keeps its targeting modes. No more than two may be deployed. Drawn as a hologram that agent skins do not change."

"An IDS monitors network activity for suspicious behaviour and security threats, then raises an alert. It watches; it does not block."
"Select FIREWALL. It is cheap, reliable, and cannot be jammed."

"Security analyst is a real job. The human in the loop takes what the automated tools flagged, works out what actually happened, and decides what to do about it. Slower than a machine, and far better on the cases that do not match a known pattern."

"Machine-learning tools flag unusual patterns across far more signals than a person can read, and are used to narrow down what deserves attention. They assist analysts rather than replace them, and they produce false positives — a flag is a lead, not a verdict."
"Three routes braid through each other twice: every lane changes side."
"Unlock this agent by reaching wave {0} on any level."

"A slow colour cycle across the whole roster."
"An IPS is an IDS with the authority to act. When it recognises an attack it drops the traffic itself instead of only telling someone about it."

"The account that can do anything on a system. Attackers want it; defenders guard it carefully. Most security work is about limiting who gets it and for how long."
"Engages up to 3 separate threats with every volley."
"{0} — {1} It deals no damage; it buys your other agents time."

"A zero-day is a flaw with no fix available yet — the defender has had zero days to patch it. Vulnerability researchers look for these so they can be reported and fixed before someone else finds them first. \"Zero-day hunter\" is informal shorthand, not a certification or a formal job title."
"Haptics on boss alerts, server hits and game over"
"Sustained damage wins. IPS or a levelled FIREWALL."

"Cyberattacks advance along network routes toward CORE-SERVER. You deploy Cyber Agents beside the lanes; they detect and destroy what comes past. Every attack you stop pays ◇ Crypto, which buys more agents and upgrades. Every fifth wave is a boss. There is no final wave — the only question is how far you get."
"+1, +10 and +100 buy that many levels. INSTALL MAX spends as much as you can afford. Each level costs a little more."
"Encryption scrambles data so only someone with the right key can read it. It protects legitimate traffic — and it equally well hides an attacker's payload from inspection."
"This build has no Google Play billing configured, or this device has no Play Store. Nothing can be bought, and nothing that costs money is required to play."

"Same flaw, no feedback. The application returns no error and no data, so the attacker asks yes-or-no questions and watches what changes — timing, page length, status codes — to read the database one bit at a time. Slow, patient, and much harder to spot in a log."

"Deals no damage and targets nothing. Repairs 1 point of CORE-SERVER integrity every 30 seconds while a wave is running (never during the break or while paused). It deploys on the CORE-SERVER itself, which has two slots for it, and nowhere else. Levels shorten the timer. No more than two may be deployed."
